name: Vocational and career coaching
summary: How trailing partners and pivoting expats evaluate career coaches in Singapore — CV localisation, interview drills, and sector mapping — without confusing coaching with licensed counselling or guaranteed job placement.
body:
Career coaches help with story, targeting, and interview performance when you are changing countries, industries, or returning to work after a trailing-spouse pause. They are not recruiters with hidden job inventories and not therapists for burnout — though good coaches will refer when mental health needs lead.

## Useful engagements
- Translating an overseas CV into Singapore-readable formats
- Interview practice for local behavioural styles
- Sector mapping when your visa status constrains roles
- LinkedIn and narrative work after a career break
- Negotiation prep once an offer appears

Beware “guaranteed EP job” packages — no ethical coach controls MOM outcomes.

## How to choose
Prefer coaches who disclose sector experience, sample session structure, and boundaries with recruitment fees. Trial one session before multi-month retainers. Ask how they handle visa-status honesty on applications. For regulated professions (teaching, clinical, legal), coaching cannot replace accreditation advice.

## How it pairs with other help
Combine with official job-search networks, professional associations, and — when anxiety or identity loss dominates — mental health resources. Dual-career households should align coaching goals with pass timelines.

## Practical tip
Bring two target role descriptions and a redacted CV to session one. Vague “help me find purpose” retainers without job targets burn cash quickly in an expensive city.
whenToEngage: Trailing partner re-entry needs CV/interview coaching
Career pivot across countries needs narrative work
Quoted guaranteed-job package needs scepticism check
Offer negotiation prep after local interviews
